texts: On day 525 of Year 2, the moon was new.
Mira led a harvest party of three people to the Salt-bloom Tide-pools at the new-moon spring tide.
The harvest party harvested nine buckets of salt-bloom.
Mira reported the harvest to the Council the next morning.

sentences: On day 525 of Year 2, the moon was new.
Mira led a harvest party of three people to the Salt-bloom Tide-pools at the new-moon spring tide.
The harvest party harvested nine buckets of salt-bloom.
Mira reported the harvest to the Council the next morning.

q1_issues.issue: The definite common-noun oblique object "the new-moon spring tide" is encoded as the bare constant new_moon_spring_tide instead of minting a witness with its kind atom, which the oblique-object NP rule requires for an article-marked NP.

(Inheritance new_moon_spring_tide tide) puts in a class position the very symbol statement 12 uses as an individual time filler, violating the individual-vs-class discipline that reserves Inheritance for kind/property on both sides.

q2_gaps: a temporal adjunct headed by "at" whose object is a definite common-noun event NP ("at the new-moon spring tide") — the Time role is specified for deictic constants, dates and clock terms, and event-noun time anchors are covered only for before/after ordering
a non-Gregorian day-of-year date ("day 525 of Year 2") — the calendar terms assume a Year/Month/Day decomposition, and nothing says whether a bare day-of-year count belongs in the (Day <n>) slot
review.notes: The rest of the passage is clean: the copular-with-time-modifier dual-emit, the collective "harvest party" (Member + GroupOf + Cardinality, no distribution rule), the unspecified-scale bucket Measure, and the no-Name treatment of "the Council" all follow the instruction set. "The next morning" emits only the day-part plus Before, which the anaphoric-time rule licenses when the antecedent event carries no day terms, though the passage's own day 525 arguably made day 526 recoverable.

issues.reason: Time's own parenthetical contrasts an event-denoting noun ('the show', 'the storm') as one that 'stays an ordinary sk_ entity', and Existential reserves the bare class symbol for non-specific/generic objects 'never for a specific definite individual', so the definite event-noun 'the new-moon spring tide' owed a witness plus its class atom rather than the bare kind symbol.

The individual/class conflation the reviewer points at is real, but it lives in statement 12's bare-symbol filler, not here: (Inheritance new_moon_spring_tide tide) is the mandatory compound-kind genus of Compound concepts, definitionally true with a kind on both sides, and survives unchanged into the compliant parse.

gaps_confirmed: no licensed filler shape for a temporal adjunct headed by 'at' whose object is a definite common-noun event NP ('at the new-moon spring tide') - Time takes structured calendar/clock terms, deictic constants and day-parts, while event-noun anchors are covered only for Before/After ordering and for During/while/throughout

no licensed term for a non-Gregorian day-of-year date ('day 525 of Year 2') - the (Day <n>) constructor is specified as a day-of-month inside a Month/Year decomposition and nothing says whether a bare day-of-year count may fill it
new_gaps: a measure-partitive container phrase ('nine buckets of salt-bloom') has no licensed positive form: Possessive/genitive NP excludes 'a cup of water' from the genitive mapping but nothing states what carries it, so the parse's (Measure sk_salt_bloom_1 unspecified 9 bucket) - a container noun as unit, 'unspecified' as scale - is unguided improvisation

the 'the next / the following morning' rule says to copy 'the antecedent's' day terms plus one, but does not say which prior eventuality is the antecedent when the immediately preceding event carries no day terms and an earlier sentence in the same passage does ('day 525' here, making day 526 arguably recoverable) - the parse's day-part-only fallback and a day-526 term are both readable off the same rule
adjudication.defect_summary: For confirmed issue 0 the compliant form mints the event-noun witness and fills the adjunct with it - (Member sk_tide_1 new_moon_spring_tide) at top level, the genus atom (Inheritance new_moon_spring_tide tide) unchanged, and the adjunct as (Time sk_lead_1 sk_tide_1) - but the Time role's filler grammar nowhere admits an entity witness and 'at' is not one of the three words that license During, so the attachment head itself has no licensed form; that is the first confirmed gap above.
adjudication.notes: The rest of the passage is sound: the copular-with-time-modifier dual-emit on 'the moon was new', the 'a flock of birds' treatment of 'a harvest party of three people', the event-anaphoric reuse of sk_harvest_1 for 'the harvest', record/report as Theme-taking verbs, and the no-Name reading of 'the Council'. The (Day 525) and 'nine buckets' improvisations are acceptable under the calibration line - every slot is traceable to the words - and are filed as gaps, not counted against the parse.
